article.headline: Games To Watch: Clarksdale girls, Palmer and Rosa Fort boys defend unbeaten starts
article.html:
Clarksdale’s unbeaten girls basketball start faces a winning Cleveland Central team Wednesday night, while Palmer and Rosa Fort try to protect perfect boys records. Those early-season tests lead a November 18 selection that also includes a district soccer matchup at Madison-Ridgeland Academy.

The basketball schedule stretches from late afternoon into the evening, with boys soccer beginning at 5 p.m. All start times below are Central Standard Time, and the records are the pregame figures listed when the matchups were checked.

Cleveland Central at Clarksdale: a winning challenger for the unbeaten Wildcats

Clarksdale’s girls enter at 4-0 for the 6 p.m. home game against Cleveland Central. The Wolves arrive at 3-1, giving the Wildcats a challenger that has also won most of its early games. Cleveland Central can hand Clarksdale its first defeat, while the Wildcats can extend their unbeaten opening against a team with only one loss. The listing identifies the game as nonconference.

West Tallahatchie at Palmer: different tests in the two varsity games

Palmer’s boys are 3-0 ahead of the 7:30 p.m. meeting in Marks, while West Tallahatchie is 0-3. The Dragons can preserve their perfect opening; the Choctaws are trying to turn their first reported victory into an interruption of that run. The contrasting records frame the matchup without making it a district standings contest: it is listed as nonconference.

The girls game is scheduled for 6 p.m. and brings a different balance. West Tallahatchie is 2-1 and Palmer is 2-2. A Choctaws win would strengthen an already winning start, while the Dragons have a chance to move above the break-even mark at home.

Rosa Fort at Riverside: Lions boys take an unbeaten start on the road

Rosa Fort’s boys carry a 3-0 record into the 7:30 p.m. game at Riverside in Avon. The Bulldogs are 2-4 and have an opportunity to challenge an unbeaten visitor on their own floor. An unbeaten visitor against a host trying to improve its opening record gives this nonconference game a clear point of interest.

In the 6 p.m. girls matchup, Riverside is 3-3 and Rosa Fort is 0-2. The Bulldogs can move to a winning record, while the Lions seek their first reported win. Riverside enters the girls game with the stronger listed record, while Rosa Fort brings the unbeaten team into the boys contest.

Edwards at Coahoma County: winning boys teams meet at 5

Coahoma County’s boys bring a 3-1 record into the 5 p.m. home game against Edwards, which is 3-2. The Panthers can improve on a start that includes only one loss, while an Edwards victory would give the Tigers a stronger winning margin in their record. Edwards travels from Ruleville to Clarksdale for the nonconference contest.

For more basketball coverage involving these schools, see our earlier Coahoma County and Riverside report.

Bayou Academy at MRA: district stakes in boys soccer

The 5 p.m. boys match at Madison-Ridgeland Academy carries a different kind of significance: MaxPreps lists it as a conference match. MRA is 1-0 overall and Bayou Academy is 1-1. The Patriots can keep their unbeaten opening intact, while the Colts can move to a winning record in a game that also matters within their conference schedule.

Washington at Heritage Academy: Patriots defend a perfect opening

Heritage Academy’s boys are 3-0 entering the 5 p.m. home match against Washington. Washington’s listing shows 0-0, so there is no reported season result to use as a form guide for the Generals. Heritage’s perfect opening supplies the reason to follow this meeting in Columbus; the match is listed as nonconference.
